page.notes: Left margin notes: "a lib.1. de ge-stis Basil. Concil." (letter a, beside the Aeneas Sylvius quotation); "b ibid." (letter b, beside the quotation "Nec considerant"); "c lib.3. de consid.cap.8." (letter c, beside "Principem Episcoporum"). The note for c reads "confid.cap.8." or "consid.cap.8.", which I could not settle; I have given "consid.cap.8.". The note for b is "ibid." and is written as a separate note in the margin. The mark for note b in the text is a small letter b before "Nec". The note letters a, b and c are shown in the text as {a}, {b}, {c} where the marks stand. Doubtful readings: "adulando" may carry an accent; "interpretetem" may be "interpretetur"; "tempofalem" is printed as such (probably a printing error for "temporalem"); there is a small mark after "Ponti-" in "Romanus Ponti-fex", probably a stain or speck, not transcribed. The first line of the page is a continuation from page 297. Right edge: a strip of the neighbouring page (text beginning "iam a", "Papa", "potel", "debat" and similar) is not transcribed.
